intro: With «se me…» you tell what happened to you by accident: something falls, breaks or is forgotten.
p.se me olvidó.glosa: I forgot it; it slipped my mind
p.se me olvidó.consejo: The forgotten thing is the subject: «se me olvidó el nombre», «se me olvidaron las llaves».
p.se me cayeron.consejo: It is plural because several things fall: «se me cayó el vaso», «se me cayeron las llaves».
p.se me rompió.consejo: «Romper» is doing it yourself; «se me rompió» says it was an accident.
p.se me perdió.glosa: I lost it; it got lost on me
p.se me perdió.consejo: The pronoun changes with the person: «se me perdió», «se te perdió», «se le perdió».
p.se me acabó.consejo: It says something ran out: «se me acabó el café». With several things: «se me acabaron».
p.se me ocurrió.consejo: It is used for ideas that arrive on their own: «se me ocurrió una idea».
p.olvidar.consejo: With «se me» it is an accident; without it you are the doer: «olvidé el paraguas».
p.caer.consejo: It is irregular: «caigo», «cae», «cayó». The y in «cayó» sounds like the y in «ya».
p.llaves.consejo: The ll sounds like the y in «yo»: YA-bes. It is feminine: «las llaves».
p.paraguas.consejo: It does not change in the plural: «el paraguas», «los paraguas». It is masculine.
p.taza.consejo: In Spain the z sounds like th: TA-tha. It is feminine: «una taza».
p.otra vez.consejo: It is written as two words. The plural of «vez» is «veces».
b1.titulo: It happened to me, by accident
b1.texto:
With **se + me / te / le / nos / os / les** you tell something that happened **by accident**.

- **Se me olvidó** el nombre. (I cannot remember it.)
- **Se me cayeron** las llaves. (They slipped out of my hands.)

The thing that falls, breaks or gets lost is the **subject**, and the verb agrees with it: one name → **olvidó**; several keys → **cayeron**.
b2.f0.texto: What is wrong with you today?
b2.f1.texto: Today I forgot the new teacher's name.
b2.f2.texto: I left my umbrella on the bus.
b2.f3.texto: This morning I dropped my keys down the stairs.
b2.f5.texto: My grandmother's favourite cup broke on me.
b2.f6.texto: And I ran out of coffee this morning.
b2.f7.texto: But I have an idea to start the day better.
b4.titulo: Who it happens to: me, te, le…
b4.texto:
The pronoun says **who** it happened to:

- to me → **se me** cayó
- to you → **se te** cayó
- to him, her, you (formal) → **se le** cayó
- to us → **se nos** cayó
- to you (plural, Spain) → **se os** cayó
- to them, you (plural) → **se les** cayó

To be clear, add **a + person**: **A Lucía** se le rompió el móvil. The verb still agrees with the thing that breaks.
b4.e0.texto: Lucía broke her cup (it broke on her).
b5.f0.texto: A jingle of metal breaks the cool silence of the stairs.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía has dropped her keys from between her sleepy fingers.
b5.f2.texto: The keys roll slowly down to the last step, like little silver moons.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía bends down, picks them up one by one and smiles without much enthusiasm.
b5.f4.texto: Upstairs, in the kitchen, the coffee runs out on her before the second cup.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo reaches the doorway without an umbrella and with his scarf askew.
b5.f6.texto: He left his umbrella on the eight o'clock bus.
b5.f7.texto: A cold drop slides down his nose and falls onto the open notebook.
b5.f8.texto: The two look at each other in silence and start laughing at so much bad luck.
b5.f9.texto: The laughter fills the doorway with a warm noise and wipes away the tiredness of the morning.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! Las llaves is plural, so the verb is too.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Cayó» is for one thing: «se me cayó el vaso».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Olvidé» says you forgot something; here they fell.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «se me» tells something that happened by accident.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «A propósito» is the opposite: you did it on purpose.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Here there is a wish, not an accident.
b7.pregunta: Choose the sentence that tells an accident.
b9.frase: A Pablo se ____ cayó el vaso.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Me» would be «a mí»: I am the one who drops the glass.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «A él» or «a Pablo» asks for «le».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Nos» would be «a nosotros»: here it is one person.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Me» only says who it happened to; it does not control the verb.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is it! Las llaves is the subject and it is plural.
b10.o2.refuerzo: There is no «yo» as the subject here: the subject is what falls.
b10.pregunta: «Se me cayeron las llaves.» What does «cayeron» agree with?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I forgot the name».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Acabaron» is plural, and «la leche» is one thing.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Acabamos» would be «nosotros acabamos»; here it is the milk that runs out.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is it! La leche is singular, so the verb is too.
p.favorita.consejo: Feminine form of «favorito», agreeing with «taza». The «v» is pronounced like «b».
p.ocurre.consejo: «Se me ocurre» means «an idea comes to me». The idea is the subject, not the person.
p.acabaron.consejo: With «se», «acabar» means that something runs out. Here, the ideas run out.
p.ideas.consejo: Plural of «idea». Its stress falls on «de», so say «i-DE-as».
p.perdieron.consejo: Past tense of «perder», for «they» lost. «Se les perdieron» means the keys got lost on them.
p.dormidos.consejo: From «dormir». Here it means fingers that feel numb, like they have fallen asleep.
p.ruedan.consejo: From «rodar». Notice that «rod-» became «rued-» in the stressed form: «RWE-dan».
p.escalón.consejo: Each «escalón» is one step of a «escalera». The «c» before «a» is a hard «k» sound.
p.lunas.consejo: Plural of «luna». In the story the keys look like small silver moons. Say «LU-nas».
p.recoge.consejo: From «recoger». The «g» before «e» sounds like a soft «j», as in «ge», so say «rre-KO-ge».
p.segunda.consejo: Feminine of «segundo». It agrees with «taza», as in «la segunda taza». Say «se-GUN-da».
p.gota.consejo: A small drop of liquid. Notice the «g» before «o» is hard, like «g» in «go».
p.reírse.consejo: Verb «reír» with «se», to laugh at something. Stress falls on «í», so say «rre-IR-se».
p.borra.consejo: From «borrar». Between vowels the «rr» is strong, like the sound of «rr» in «perro».
p.cayeron.consejo: Past tense of «caer», for several things falling. Say «ka-YE-ron», with «ye» as one sound.
p.cayó.consejo: Past tense of «caer», for one thing. The accent on «ó» marks the stress: «ka-YO».
p.acabó.consejo: Past tense of «acabar» with a single subject. Stress falls on «ó»: «a-ka-BO».
